issues.title: Beacon truth leaks through three unauthenticated endpoints
issues.problem: Hub.snapshot() is the only place truth is filtered and only /api/state and /ws use it. GET /api/scenarios returns every beacon_lat/lon; GET /api/sorties/{id}/track returns `beacon` for a running unrevealed sortie; snapshot() pops lat/lon but leaves beacon_elev_ft. Any participant reads the answer in one request, defeating the design's core teaching mechanism.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08: one public_scenario() serializer in main.py strips beacon_lat/lon/elev_ft unless truth is explicitly allowed; /api/scenarios returns truth only for a presented instructor token; /api/sorties/{id}/track returns beacon only once that sortie is revealed, and now also reports `revealed` so the debrief's 'never revealed' branch is reachable. Regression test tests/test_console.py walks every scenario/sortie response for a value within ~100 m of truth.
issues.verify: Automated test: with a running unrevealed sortie, no response body from any GET endpoint contains a coordinate within 100 m of truth.

issues.title: Plugin can never receive beacon truth, so the in-sim DF is deaf
issues.problem: The plugin polls /api/state, which withholds truth until reveal, then sets active=1 with lat/lon at 0/0 or the previous exercise's beacon. Distance to Null Island exceeds the radio horizon, so the authoritative DF engine produces nothing for the whole exercise unless the instructor reveals at the start.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08, both halves. Console: GET /api/plugin/scenario returns the running sortie with truth, gated on CAPVSAR_TOKEN_PLUGIN, 503 when no key is configured so it cannot be open by accident. Plugin: net_worker now polls that endpoint with the key (PLUGIN_KEY, from CAPVSAR_TOKEN_PLUGIN; O-2 will move it into the station config alongside CONSOLE and CALLSIGN) and sends the same key on /api/positions, which is now gated too. A refused channel (403/503/404) clears scn['active'] so the DF goes silent instead of homing on a null beacon, and logs the reason once per transition.
issues.verify: tests/test_plugin_net.py (9 checks) covers the endpoint choice, the key header, and each refusal path; tests/test_console.py asserts the payload carries every field the plugin reads. Still to confirm in the sim: a bearing appears on the DF head during an unrevealed sortie.

issues.title: Terrain line-of-sight ray is mirrored
issues.problem: interp() walks aircraft to beacon with `fr`, but `ray = b_ft + (ac_ft - b_ft) * fr` puts the beacon's altitude at the aircraft end. Ridges near the beacon never block; high ground near the aircraft falsely blocks. Terrain masking — a headline training effect — is inverted.
issues.fix: ray = ac_ft + (b_ft - ac_ft) * fr.
issues.verify: New test with a non-flat terrain stub (ridge at 30/60/90 % of path) asserting blocked vs clear in both directions.

issues.title: No authentication or role separation on any console endpoint
issues.problem: Any LAN/WireGuard participant can stop a sortie, reveal the beacon, delete scenarios or rewrite injected effects. Only the radio stream has an access code and it defaults to empty. /ws has no origin check although the radio socket does.
issues.fix: Superseded 2026-09-08 by the full Exercise Setup / RBAC system (services/exercise/app/access.py): session-cookie and QR/short-code participant login (/join/<code>, /login) with a roster generated per exercise by the Setup wizard, role tokens (instructor/base/aircrew/ground_team/plugin) enforced on every mutating route and view, instructor satisfies base, /ws origin-checked. The old CAPVSAR_TOKEN_* shared-secret env vars are preserved only for backward compatibility with the plugin/scripts, not required for participant roles — the earlier REMAINING item (setting those on ms01) no longer gates this fix. Covered by tests/test_setup_auth.py (23 tests) and tests/test_console.py::RoleGates.
issues.verify: A non-instructor session (base/aircrew/ground_team) gets 403 on reveal/stop/scenario mutation; /setup and / redirect unauthenticated or non-instructor sessions; /join/<code> and /login establish a working session cookie. Covered by tests/test_setup_auth.py and tests/test_console.py::RoleGates.

issues.title: Fresh deploy crash-loops; repo is not the deployment
issues.problem: Sharpened 2026-09-08. Confirmed: scripts/deploy.sh creates only mumble/data. Compose also bind-mounts services/exercise/data, services/flightplanner/data/aviation_data.db (as a FILE) and services/exercise/radio-public - none of which deploy.sh creates and all correctly gitignored as runtime state. So a fresh clone plus deploy.sh still crash-loops the flight planner: Docker materialises the missing aviation_data.db path as a directory and sqlite3.connect fails at import. The live ms01 stack works only because those paths were created by hand at some earlier point.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. scripts/deploy.sh now creates every host path compose bind-mounts - services/exercise/data, services/exercise/radio-public and services/flightplanner/data/charts - and touches aviation_data.db as an empty file, which SQLite accepts. The file case is the one that mattered: Docker silently creates a missing DIRECTORY mount, but for a FILE mount it creates a directory where the file belongs, which is why gunicorn crash-looped. It also publishes Caddy's root CA into radio-public, a step nobody had scripted - Caddy mints it into a named volume the console cannot read, so /radio-ca.crt served nothing anywhere the file had not been hand-copied.
issues.verify: Verified by cloning the repo to a temp dir on ms01 and running the real script against a stubbed docker: four paths created, the 0-byte database accepted by sqlite3, the CA published, second run idempotent. Committed 0e2e0d1 (amended). NOT yet proven end-to-end with a real `docker compose up` on a clean host - that needs a spare machine.

issues.title: Plugin hardcodes console address and callsign — multi-aircraft not deployable
issues.problem: Corrected 2026-09-08: participant onboarding is NOT absent. The canonical repo has docs/CONNECT.md (join guide), scripts/wg-peer.sh (prints a WireGuard peer config and QR for a named participant), scripts/deploy.sh (idempotent stack deploy) and infra/ROUTER.md. What remains real and unchanged: the plugin hardcodes CONSOLE and CALLSIGN with no per-station override, so three aircraft still means three hand-edited copies; the deploy scripts are Linux-only; build_c182t_package.py hardcodes /home/ron; and there is no single station kit bundling plugin + instruments + panel + aircraft + CA cert for a member to install.
issues.fix: xplane/PI_capvsar_df.py now loads CONSOLE/CALLSIGN/PLUGIN_KEY from capvsar_station.ini beside wherever the plugin is deployed (_load_station_config()), falling back independently per-key to the historical single-station defaults so an install with no ini is unchanged. CAPVSAR_TOKEN_PLUGIN still overrides the ini plugin_key. scripts/build_station_kit.py generates a per-station kit (plugin + generated ini + the four Air Manager instruments + a README), optionally zipped. The tracked plugin source is now byte-identical across every station, so deploy_xplane_plugin.py hash checks mean something again. NOT bundled, deliberately: the C182T aircraft package (build_c182t_package.py derives it from the recipient's own local Laminar install, not redistributable) and a CA certificate (issued per ms01 deployment, not present in this repo).
issues.verify: tests/test_engine.py: _load_station_config() falls back to defaults with no ini, applies per-key overrides from an ini, and confirms CAPVSAR_TOKEN_PLUGIN beats the ini. End-to-end: scripts/build_station_kit.py --callsign CAP-2 built a kit, and importing that kit's PI_capvsar_df.py directly (own directory, own ini) yielded CALLSIGN=CAP-2 and the kit's plugin_key — the same tracked source picking up a different station identity from its own directory. Deployed via scripts/deploy_xplane_plugin.py to this machine's X-Plane install (no station.ini present there, so behavior is unchanged from before this fix).

issues.title: Mumble channel tree exists only as hand-made rows in a runtime volume
issues.problem: Corrected twice. The channel tree exists on ms01 (hand-inserted into mumble-server.sqlite) AND is documented in docs/MUMBLE_CHANNELS.md, which gives the full tree, the rationale, and the one manual step still outstanding: the ACL on the Instructor/SET channel denying Enter. So this is neither undocumented nor a first-join failure. What remains real: the rows live only in a gitignored runtime volume with nothing in the repo to recreate them, radio.py carries its own hardcoded copy of four names, and the instructor-channel ACL is still a manual step per the doc.
issues.fix: services/exercise/app/mumble_channels.py is now the single source of truth for the tree (docs/MUMBLE_CHANNELS.md); radio.py imports its CHANNELS from it instead of an independent hardcoded copy. scripts/provision_mumble.py recreates the whole tree idempotently by inspecting ms01's live mumble-server.sqlite schema directly (Murmur has no config-file channel definition) and also finishes the previously-manual Instructor/SET ACL: deny Enter to @all, grant Enter+Speak to a new @instructor group, at ACL priorities 0/1 so the grant overrides the deny per mumble.info/documentation/administration/acl. scripts/deploy.sh now stops mumble, runs the provisioner, restarts it, on every deploy. Also caught and fixed a real naming drift: the doc's own tree diagram said "Instructor / SET" while its setup steps and the live database both said "Instructor - SET".
issues.verify: tests/test_provision_mumble.py, 4 cases, built against ms01's actual live schema (inspected via docker cp + sqlite3, not assumed): a brand-new server gets the whole tree; the Instructor/SET ACL rows land with correct priority and permission bits; an already hand-provisioned tree (ms01's real state) is left byte-for-byte untouched aside from the two new ACL rows; running twice changes nothing the second time. NOT yet run against ms01's actual live mumble-server.sqlite - that needs stopping the live voice server and was left for explicit sign-off.

issues.title: X-Plane .fms export is malformed
issues.problem: The v1100 waypoint line is `type ident airway|DRCT altitude lat lon`; the code emits `11 SS01 5500.0 lat lon`, dropping DRCT so the altitude is parsed as the airway. Type 11 means a named fix in the navdata, but SS01/DATUM do not exist. CYCLE 2401 is hardcoded. The test asserts the broken format, locking it in.
issues.fix: Emit type 28 with a +lat_lon ident and the DRCT column for user waypoints; derive CYCLE from the date; fix the test to assert the real format.
issues.verify: Load an exported pattern in X-Plane 12 and fly the first two legs from the G1000 flight plan page.

issues.title: Scan mode destroys TIMEHOLD on 406
issues.problem: Scan steps the receiver to alt1/alt2 between bursts; the next tick finds it untuned and calls silent(), clearing `held`. With scan_enable=1 — the 517's normal 406 posture — the bearing vanishes the instant each 440 ms burst ends instead of holding, which is exactly the behaviour the training relies on.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. The untuned path now distinguishes scan stepping from being parked on the wrong channel. When scan has stepped off the crew's channel between bursts it calls silent(keep_hold=True) then hold_or_drop(), the same treatment the between-bursts gap already got, so TIMEHOLD carries the bearing across the step. Tuning away by hand still drops it. Added tuned_hz() so 'what the crew selected' and 'what the receiver is on this instant' are separate questions rather than duplicated logic.
issues.verify: New test: 406 beacon with scan enabled holds a bearing between bursts.

issues.title: Radio horizon is one-sided
issues.problem: Uses sqrt(max(alt - beacon_elev, 0)), which is zero when the aircraft is below the beacon: an aircraft in a valley 500 ft below a ridge-top beacon 1 NM away hears nothing.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. Both ends of the path now raise the horizon: 1.23*(sqrt(h_ac)+sqrt(h_bcn)) in feet MSL, in the plugin and in the server's propagation.py fallback, kept identical. The old form used the aircraft's height above the beacon, which went to zero the moment the beacon sat higher - an aircraft in a valley below a ridge-top beacon 1 NM away was ruled out of range. Terrain between the two remains a separate question, answered by the LOS probe.
issues.verify: Test with the aircraft below beacon elevation at 1 NM: signal present.

issues.title: Plugin disable/enable cycle kills the console link permanently
issues.problem: XPluginDisable sets self.stop and never clears it, so the thread started by XPluginEnable exits immediately. Datarefs keep publishing stale state with no console link and no error.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. XPluginEnable creates a fresh threading.Event, so a disable/enable cycle no longer starts a worker that exits on its first check. XPluginDisable joins with a 1 s timeout - bounded because the worker may be inside a 4 s urlopen and X-Plane must not block on it; it is a daemon and the event is set, so it exits regardless.
issues.verify: Reload the plugin in X-Plane; positions resume on /base.

issues.title: SQLite writes block the event loop that carries radio audio
issues.problem: Synchronous sqlite3 calls inside async handlers share the loop with 20 ms PCM frames for the Mumble bridge. Every commit fsyncs on a bind mount; a stalled commit trips the audio buffer check and unkeys the operator mid-transmission. No WAL, no timeout, connections never closed.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. db() is now a context manager that commits, rolls back and CLOSES (it leaked a connection per request), opens with timeout=5s, and the database is in WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL. Every write in an async handler now goes through db_call() -> run_in_threadpool, so no commit runs on the loop carrying the Mumble bridge's 20 ms frames. The sync handlers were already threadpooled by FastAPI. Only startup seeding still touches the database on the loop, before any traffic.
issues.verify: Hold PTT while an instructor starts a sortie and logs bearings: no audio dropout, no 'connection delayed' notice.

issues.title: Console restart mid-exercise orphans the sortie
issues.problem: hub.sortie/scenario/aircraft/messages live only in process and are never rehydrated from SQLite on startup. After a restart the plugin's positions are discarded, /api/messages returns empty because it reads memory not the table, and the DB row keeps stopped=NULL forever.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. rehydrate() runs in lifespan: the most recent sortie with stopped IS NULL is reloaded with its scenario and last 100 messages. Aircraft are deliberately NOT restored - their positions are seconds stale and plugins re-report within seconds; a stale aircraft on the map is worse than a briefly empty one.
issues.verify: Restart the container mid-sortie: aircraft reappear and the sortie can still be stopped and revealed.

issues.title: One wedged WebSocket client stalls every broadcast
issues.problem: Hub.broadcast awaits send_text sequentially with no timeout, so one wedged tablet blocks the 1 Hz ticker and every HTTP handler that broadcasts. Half-open sockets never raise and are never dropped.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. broadcast() now sends to all clients concurrently with a 1 s per-client timeout (Hub.SEND_TIMEOUT_S) and drops anyone who times out or raises. A half-open socket never raises, so a timeout rather than an exception is what notices it.
issues.verify: Suspend a tablet mid-exercise; other consoles keep updating.

issues.title: Base view keeps the previous sortie's alert circle and tracks
issues.problem: alertCircle is created once and never updated or removed and `centred` never resets; trackLines/bearingLayer are never cleared on a new sortie. Base staff plot against the previous scenario's search area. Expired aircraft also leak their trackLines entry.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. base.js now tracks the sortie id from the state snapshot and calls clearSortieLayers() when it changes, removing the alert circle and its marker (the marker was never even held in a variable), the beacon marker, aircraft markers, tracks and bearings, and resetting `centred`. Also fixed a leak the review only half-described: when an aircraft went quiet for 30 s and came back, a NEW polyline replaced trackLines[callsign] and orphaned the old one on the map permanently - it now resumes the existing track instead. An expired aircraft's marker is removed but its flown track is deliberately kept, because that is history base staff still need.
issues.verify: Verified by driving a real browser session through two sorties over CDP: with the fix, tracks and bearings go to 0 and map layers drop 9 -> 5; against pre-F-2 code the previous sortie's track and bearing survive (tracks 1, bearings 1, layers 9 -> 7).

issues.title: Debrief conflates all aircraft into one track
issues.problem: /track returns callsign per position but the debrief treats them as one track: with three aircraft the polyline zigzags between them, 'track flown' sums inter-aircraft jumps and closest approach is meaningless — the scoring the SET relies on. Heading is also derived via atan2(dlon, dlat) with no cos(lat), ~10 deg bias at 33 N, although hdg_true is stored and simply not returned.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08, both halves. Server: /api/sorties/{id}/track now returns hdg_true, which was stored on every position and discarded by the query. Client: debrief.js groups positions by callsign - one faint full track, one playback polyline and one labelled marker per aircraft, each in its own colour - and scores each aircraft separately for closest approach, track flown, direct line and efficiency. Heading uses the recorded hdg_true when present, and the fallback now scales longitude by cos(latitude), which the old inline calculation omitted (~10 deg of error at 33N).
issues.verify: Verified in a headless browser against a seeded three-aircraft sortie (180 positions): three separate scored rows - CAP-1 0.00 nm 'overhead the beacon', CAP-2 3.34 nm 'did not close', CAP-3 1.96 nm 'localised' - three labelled markers, no JS errors. tests/test_console.py covers the hdg_true half.

issues.title: Radio console does not rejoin after a network blip
issues.problem: The radio deliberately does not auto-reconnect, so a Wi-Fi blip silently drops the base station off the voice net with only a text notice. Base and legacy reconnect but lose bearings and messages broadcast during the outage: messages are fetched only at page load and bearings have no list endpoint at all.
issues.fix: Rejoin with backoff plus an audible alarm on the radio; add GET /api/bearings?since= and ?since= on messages; refetch on reconnect.
issues.verify: Drop the tablet's Wi-Fi for 30 s: the radio rejoins audibly and the base view backfills what it missed.

issues.title: Unauthenticated scenario push and CSRF-able database wipe
issues.problem: /api/sar/export-vsar has no auth or rate limit and its free-text fields flow unbounded into scenario name/notes/alert_text and a broadcast to every console. /api/update-database takes no body, so a plain cross-site form POST triggers a DB wipe and reload. The README still advertises Cloud Run --allow-unauthenticated.
issues.fix: Require the base token on the push; JSON-only with a CSRF-safe method on update-database; length caps on all free text.
issues.verify: Unauthenticated push returns 401; a cross-site form POST to update-database is rejected.

issues.title: Parallel-track generator can be driven into a 100M-iteration loop
issues.problem: num_legs is capped and spacing floored, but length_nm/width_nm are unbounded: width_nm=1e7 with spacing 0.1 is 1e8 sweeps, from an endpoint reachable without auth.
issues.fix: Cap width and length (<= 60 NM) and total legs.
issues.verify: Oversized request returns 400 quickly.

issues.title: Both gunicorn workers race to rebuild the aviation database
issues.problem: auto_update_if_empty() runs at import in both workers, so two threads concurrently DELETE/INSERT the same SQLite file; lock errors are swallowed by bare except: pass, silently dropping rows. update_status is per-process so /api/update-status answers inconsistently.
issues.fix: Do the update once (a CLI command or a lock file); log exceptions instead of swallowing them.
issues.verify: Cold start with an empty DB twice: row counts match the source both times.

issues.title: DF faceplates repaint ~8 Hz regardless of change
issues.problem: The 250 ms tick repaints unconditionally and df.on_change fires redraw() from all three subscription groups every engine tick — roughly 8 Hz of ~100 _txt calls each rebuilding a style string, whether anything changed or not. This is CPU the MO station spends for nothing and it widens the canvas_draw reentrancy window.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. In cap_df.lua and DF heads' logic.lua, added snapshot-based change detection so redraw only occurs on whole-second timer boundaries or true bearing/signal/flag state changes, eliminating ~8 Hz idle repaint load.
issues.verify: Air Manager CPU drops measurably with a static signal; display still updates within 250 ms of a real change.

issues.title: pcall around canvas_draw hides real errors
issues.problem: The pcall was added for a reentrancy error the Air Manager log shows only twice, each immediately followed by the missing-callback signature that was separately fixed — and zero occurrences since. It now silently swallows every synchronous canvas_draw failure.
issues.fix: Fixed 2026-09-08. Dropped the swallowing pcall around canvas_draw in both becker-sar-df-517/logic.lua and rhotheta-rt-600/logic.lua.
issues.verify: Exercise pages 1-3 and scan mode; Air Manager log stays clean.

issues.title: Mumble server has no per-role ACLs and images float
issues.problem: CERTREQUIRED=false, ALLOWHTML=true, a single shared server password, no channel ACLs, USERS=100, and mumble-server:latest / caddy:2 unpinned. The radio console's callsign is free-form, so a student can present as MISSION BASE on the net.
issues.fix: Images pinned by digest to what was already running and tested on ms01 (mumblevoip/mumble-server, caddy:2) - not "latest" silently drifting under a live voice net. Per-role channel ACLs on Instructor/SET are provision_mumble.py's work, shared with O-4 (same mechanism, same script). radio.py's /api/radio/stream now derives the callsign from an authenticated RBAC session (access.get_session_from_request) when one exists, ignoring whatever the client claims - a base-role student can no longer type "MISSION BASE" or "INSTRUCTOR" and impersonate another station. No session (RBAC not configured for the exercise) falls back to the client-supplied callsign as before, matching access.py's fail-open design elsewhere. CERTREQUIRED=false, ALLOWHTML=true and USERS=100 were NOT changed - those are the training net's deliberate low-friction-join posture, not oversights, and changing them wasn't asked for or verified against real join friction.
issues.verify: tests/test_radio.py: two new cases - an authenticated session's callsign overrides a conflicting client-claimed one; no session falls back to the client-supplied callsign unchanged. issues.title: No backup, monitoring or pre-exercise smoke check
issues.problem: ms01 carries all services, the SQLite database and the voice bridge; the router carries everyone's WireGuard; there is no backup of exercise.db, no monitoring, and radio-https has no healthcheck. An exercise-day failure loses the record with no warning.
issues.fix: scripts/preflight.py checks the exercise console's /api/health, the full Mumble channel tree plus the Instructor/SET ACL (reading the shared mumble_channels.py tree, same source O-4 provisions from), the flight planner's VFR tile source via the MapServer metadata endpoint (not a guessed tile coordinate - a 404 on an out-of-pyramid tile looks identical to the service being down otherwise), and the published browser-radio CA cert. scripts/backup_exercise_db.py takes an online SQLite backup (Connection.backup(), safe against a live writer - not a raw file copy, which can capture a torn snapshot) with 14-day retention pruning; a crontab line is in the script's own docstring, not installed anywhere by this change. radio-https (Caddy) gained a healthcheck in docker-compose.yml - it had none, so a Caddy that stopped proxying looked identical to a healthy one to `docker compose ps`. Nightly cron installed on ms01 (03:00, backs up to /mnt/nfs3/capvsar/backups/exercise-db - NFS3, the WD NAS at 192.0.2.144, mounted on ms01 for this specifically; it had no client mount before this). backup() gained retry-on-transient-failure after the first live run against that fresh mount hit exactly the kind of one-off I/O error a network destination can produce, with no retry of its own in sqlite3's backup API.
issues.verify: preflight.py manually run against both a cold stack (nothing running: fails loudly, one specific reason per check) and a fully mocked warm one (provisioned test Mumble db, mock health server, placeholder CA cert: all five checks pass) - the tracker's own stated verify criterion. tests/test_backup_exercise_db.py, 4 cases, caught a real bug during development: same-second backups collided on a 1-second-resolution filename and silently overwrote each other, fixed by moving to microsecond resolution. issues.fix: Publish the gated value; evaluate squelch against it.

issues.title: Terrain masking is only -12 dB
issues.problem: Blocked paths attenuate by *0.06, so a fully masked beacon at 2 NM still yields signal 0.375 and a valid bearing. Real knife-edge diffraction loss is 20-40 dB, so the masking effect barely teaches anything inside ~4 NM.
issues.fix: Deepen the loss to a realistic knife-edge range and recheck the existing masking tests.

issues.title: Fixed 24 terrain probes, no earth curvature
issues.problem: 24 probes means 1.25 NM spacing at 30 NM, skipping narrow ridges, and the straight ray ignores the ~200 ft mid-path curvature bulge at that range.
issues.fix: Scale probe count with distance; add the curvature term.
issues.verify: A narrow ridge at 25 NM blocks.

issues.title: DATAREF_CONTRACT.md does not match what the plugin publishes
issues.problem: The contract is the interface between the plugin and every faceplate, and it is wrong in five places: cap/scenario/* is documented writable for offline testing but active is read-only; bearing extremes are documented as +/- spread/2 but published one-sided; 'slant range' is ground great-circle; BYTE[15] returns length 0 undecoded; and five effect names are undocumented.

issues.problem: The server model uses a 1.5 s burst window against the plugin's 0.44 s, never invalidates between bursts, matches band as the string '406', and has no squelch, averaging, timehold, tuning, terrain or airframe modelling. It runs whenever the plugin omits df, so an instructor can be shown a different DF picture than the sim computes.
issues.fix: Shrink propagation.py to the mock-bridge stub it effectively is and make the plugin authoritative everywhere, per existing policy.
issues.verify: Instructor HUD matches the cockpit in a sim-connected exercise.

issues.title: Plugin reporting cadence and heading source are off
issues.problem: REPORT_S=2 but the loop sleeps 3 s; the first report is (0,0,0) before any flight loop; psi is the OpenGL-frame heading where true_psi is correct; a null in scenario JSON would throw in the dataref accessor.
issues.fix: Align the sleep with REPORT_S, skip the first empty report, use true_psi, coerce nulls.
issues.verify: Track starts at the aircraft's real position with 2 s spacing.

issues.title: Signal model has no dB calibration and multipath is scripted
issues.problem: 25/d^2 saturates at 5 NM for every band, so a 0.1 W 121.5 beacon and a 5 W 406 beacon differ only in cadence and decode, not range. Multipath is a deterministic 40 deg step for 12 of every 36 s, independent of terrain or range, so it reads as a scripted glitch rather than a reflection.
issues.fix: Calibrate to a real link budget per band; drive multipath from the terrain probe that already runs.
issues.verify: Detection ranges differ per band and match published ELT figures within a training tolerance.

issues.title: Untyped request bodies mutate scenario definitions

Creeping line silently truncates at max_legs with no warning that coverage is incomplete. heading_mag is emitted for expanding square but not the other two.

issues.title: Performance tables extrapolate silently and ignore tailwind
issues.problem: get_cruise is nearest-neighbour rather than interpolating; takeoff/landing clamp to the last table row, understating distance above 6000 ft or 30 C; negative headwind (tailwind) is ignored; and when wind >= TAS ground speed clamps to zero and the leg then reports zero time and fuel, so an impossible leg looks cheap.
issues.fix: Implemented: interpolate cruise altitude/RPM between supported rows; reject beyond-table cruise and runway altitude/temperature. Apply C172S POH tailwind correction (+10% per 2 kt through 10 kt); refuse stronger tailwind. Non-positive GS and unmaintainable crosswind raise errors; route HTTP 400 names the leg. Tests cover 100 kt headwind at 90 KTAS, tailwind, interpolation and out-of-table inputs.
issues.verify: A leg with a 100 kt headwind reports an error, not zero fuel.

issues.title: Flight planner plans a different aircraft than the exercise flies
issues.problem: Re-scoped 2026-09-10 after Codex correctly stopped on the original wording. The old description said the planner holds 172S figures 'under a 182T label'. It does not - app.py:80 says 'N499CP - Cessna 172S NAV III' and the planner README and USER_GUIDE agree, so the profile is labelled honestly. The real defect is an identity collision: N499CP is a REAL Cessna 172S on the squadron line, and the simulated aircraft was wearing that same registration while being a 182T. Fixed on the simulator side 2026-09-10 - the simulated aircraft is now CAP 487 (3100 lb, 87 gal, IO-540) everywhere except this planner. What is left is the planning gap the original item was really about: the exercise flies CAP 487 and the planner computes fuel, endurance and W&B for a 172S, so every sortie is planned on the wrong airframe. The crew no longer even matches on a shared registration. Source check 2026-09-10: Cessna 182TIMBUS-01 (20 Dec 2007), section 6-8 and figure 6-3, requires aircraft-specific empty weight and moment; its sample is 1924 lb and 70.9 thousand lb-in. The builder sets CAP 487 to 1970 lb but supplies no corresponding POH-datum empty moment or documented conversion from the inherited X-Plane CG. The planner requires empty_weight_moment. Implementation stopped under the prompt's no-guessing rule; obtain or explicitly define the simulated aircraft's datum-referenced W&B record before adding the complete profile. Source: https://www.aeroelectric.com/Reference_Docs/Cessna/cessna-poh/C182T_2007_NavIII-G1000%2BGFC700_POH-PIM_fromCessna.pdf .
issues.fix: Implemented 2026-09-10 after the user explicitly selected POH numbers. CAP 487 is the default with the C182T POH SAMPLE empty weight/moment (1924 lb / 70.9 thousand lb-in), 3100 lb takeoff, 2950 lb landing and 87 gal usable. Imported cited standard-temperature altitude/RPM/manifold-pressure cruise tables, climb, runway and CG/arm data. UI includes manifold pressure, correct weights/fuel/reference and a visible sample-baseline note. Old N499CP profile removed. Builder still uses 1970 lb and its CG datum is unverified: tracked separately in L-7a, with no claim that a planner update modified the simulator.
issues.verify: 32 planner tests and 49 console/radio tests pass. At 6000 ft / 2400 RPM / 20 inHg, reproduces POH 65%, 130 KTAS and 11.4 GPH; full 87 gal with start/climb and 45-minute reserve gives 6.66 h, consistent with handbook 5.5+ h. UI defaults and CG envelope breakpoints tested. No X-Plane flight verification.

issues.title: Flight planner database is a file bind-mount, so SQLite journals escape it
issues.problem: Found while fixing O-3. Compose mounts aviation_data.db as a single FILE at /app/aviation_data.db. SQLite writes its rollback journal beside the database, so -journal and -wal files land in the container's own /app layer rather than on the host. A crash mid-write leaves the journal on a discarded layer and the database with no way to roll back. O-3 works around the symptom by pre-creating the file; this is the underlying shape.
issues.fix: Mount the DIRECTORY - ./services/flightplanner/data:/app/data - and point DATABASE_PATH at /app/data/aviation_data.db so the journal stays with the database. The host file does not move, so no migration. Left for Codex because app.py is its lane and it had uncommitted work there.
issues.verify: A write leaves its journal on the host volume, not inside the container.

issues.problem: The supervised airborne maneuver gate and X-Plane adapter are covered by packet-level tests, but live CAP 487 handling, G1000/GFC 700 annunciations, capture, pilot takeover, pause, and disconnect behavior remain unverified. The 2026-09-11 acceptance attempt could not start X-Plane because NVIDIA userspace 595.91.07 did not match the loaded 595.84 kernel module.
issues.fix: 2026-09-11: live heading capture (12.742 s), FLC altitude capture (50.555 s), out-of-block command refusal, pilot takeover, old-lease refusal and shutdown pause verified. User confirmed FLC-to-ALT, AP disconnect and shutdown pause. Corrected telemetry-loss trial dropped 48 packets for 5.007 s: stale telemetry revoked lease in 1.900 s after drop began, pause_on passed through, direct pause readback=1. Telemetry recovered without reacquisition and old lease returned HTTP 400. Controller/relay stopped and subscriptions cancelled. Initial loss trial was invalid due to old direct subscriptions and remains documented. AI-2 stays open for installed CAP 487 package verification (AI-4); manual recovery verified by user report and four seconds of live pause=0, altitude 4199.636 ft, 122.422 KIAS, bank 0.576 degrees and VVI -0.224 ft/min. Explicit visual confirmation of the latest automatic fault pause has not been supplied; direct telemetry proved pause=1. AI-4 package has now been corrected and installed with static validation; fresh X-Plane load and visual cockpit verification remain pending. Direct surface-control backend and card H0 campaign 2026-09-11: added services/ai_pilot/direct_backend.py (XPlaneDirectBackend), which flies the primary flight controls rather than the GFC 700 and so covers aircraft with no autopilot, implemented against the EXISTING maneuvers.FlightBackend protocol so the lease, sequence, envelope and capture detection all still apply; maneuvers.py was NOT modified and the gate was never bypassed. Extended along the axes the handling cards need: apply_test_input (H0, bounded/ramped/self-expiring single-axis inputs), select_bank (H2), select_airspeed for speed-on-pitch (H1/H3), set_flaps (H4) and elevator trim. Card H0 (control and trim confidence, 100 KIAS clean) was attempted FIVE times and remains UNFLOWN - it has not yet reached its first control input from a stabilized reference condition. Each attempt terminated on a different real control-law defect, all five now fixed and locked by offline tests, none of which the pre-existing 53 offline tests caught: (1) step test inputs and no turn coordination, fixed with a trapezoidal ramp and sideslip PI; (2a) throttle bang-bang 0.150-1.000 swinging speed 94.7-108.8 about a 100 target, caused by a PURE INTEGRATOR at 0.1 throttle/sec/knot, fixed with PI; (2b) a standing sideslip through the climb that the heading loop masked by holding +1.6 deg of right bank, fixed with a right-rudder feedforward scaling with throttle and inversely with dynamic pressure; (3) an abrupt roll that was NOT the input - the ramp was verified correct on the trace, climbing 0.0077 to 0.1000 over exactly 1.0 s with the aileron tracking to four decimals - but a STEP IN THE RECOVERY, where the heading loop commanded the aileron limit in a single 100 ms tick the instant the input expired, held it saturated 1.2 s, reached 14.3 deg/s and overshot from -20.7 to +9.2 deg; fixed with rate damping on both inner loops and a slew-rate limiter on all three surfaces applied last before the wire (a ramped input passes through untouched at 0.10/s against a 0.40 limit). Run 3 was ALSO not a valid test point: it entered 22 knots fast, the throttle went to the idle stop and the integral wound to its -0.35 limit for ten seconds where integrating could not change the output, then had to unwind off the stop, so speed sailed through the target to 94.1 KIAS in a 274 fpm descent - the condition the first input was flown from; fixed with conditional integration, since clamping the integral TERM is not anti-windup. (4) Added a criteria-based stabilization gate to scripts/fly_card_h0.py (kias +/-2, alt +/-60 ft, vs +/-120 fpm, bank +/-2 deg, held 4 s continuous, 120 s timeout, exit 3 on failure, --force stamps the run as invalid), which immediately caught the aircraft sitting 107 ft low for two full minutes at 100.0 KIAS, -3 fpm and -0.2 deg bank, correcting none of it: a pure proportional cascade reaches equilibrium the moment pitch equals its command, which it can do at a standing altitude error because the pitch the VS loop asks for at that error is also the attitude that flies level - every loop satisfied with the aircraft in the wrong place; fixed with a bounded, conditionally-integrated altitude trim term, without which the card's reference condition is not reachable and the card cannot be flown at all. (5) The backend engaged on an aircraft the autopilot had left trimmed to +0.432 nose-up and held full nose-DOWN elevator saturated at -0.400 for seven seconds while the aircraft pitched UP to 11.5 deg and climbed at 1,533 fpm, terminating on the gate's own 90 KIAS floor; nothing in the control law was wrong, it had no trim authority and no way to know it was out-trimmed, because a saturated surface and a slow one look identical from the response alone. docs/C182T_HANDLING_TEST_MATRIX.md had listed 'no trim' as a BLOCKED reason for H0 before any of this was flown. Fixed with an autotrim loop that adopts the aircraft's real trim by readback and WILL NOT WRITE TRIM IT HAS NOT FIRST MEASURED, frozen during a pitch test input, and kept out of CONTROL_DREFS so release leaves the aircraft trimmed rather than slamming trim to neutral. CORRECTION to the pre-flight assessment: the matrix named capture rate as the instrumentation risk; it was not. The real gap was that a saturated surface and a slow one are indistinguishable from the response alone, so three of the five defects were invisible until COMMANDED SURFACE POSITIONS were logged beside the response. Traces now record the pre-rate-limit demand next to each issued command, trim position and trim RATE, all integrator states, and body_rate_age_s (inf when the damping terms were flown as zero for want of data) so a zero meaning 'not rolling' and a zero meaning 'no data' never look alike. Body rates and trim are auxiliary datarefs held OUTSIDE the freshness gate, so losing a damping channel degrades the damping rather than neutralizing the controls on an airborne aircraft. After run 5 the aircraft was left at 77 KIAS at full power out of trim; recovered by direct write to 81.4 KIAS at 3,908 ft and the pilot paused the simulator. Procedural finding: run 5 engaged during a transient left by the previous run's release, and the entry check tested envelope compliance only, not steadiness. Handling cards now: H0 unblocked but UNFLOWN, H2 unblocked 90-110 KIAS and blocked at 80, H3 and H4 unblocked and unflown, H1 and H5-H7 still BLOCKED on the gate's 90 KIAS floor - which is the specific guard against an autonomous system flying to the stall and is NOT recommended for removal. services/ai_pilot/tests/test_direct_backend.py is now 80 offline tests (from 53), the ai_pilot suite 150, none requiring X-Plane. NOTHING here is recorded as a handling pass or fail, no gain is validated, and none of it validates the aircraft or closes A-1. Full findings with trace evidence in docs/C182T_H0_CONTROL_LAW_FINDINGS.md.

issues.title: Literal codes ADMIN and INSTRUCTOR mint an instructor session without the token
issues.problem: authenticate_code() treats the literal strings ADMIN and INSTRUCTOR as valid participant codes whenever CAPVSAR_TOKEN_INSTRUCTOR is set in the environment. It checks only that the token EXISTS; it never compares the caller's input against it. GET /join/ADMIN is therefore a plain unauthenticated URL that mints an Exercise Director session, sets the cookie and redirects to /. Because instructor satisfies every other role in SATISFIED_BY, this grants sortie control, scenario deletion, effects injection and truth reveal. It defeats X-1: that fix gates beacon_lat/lon behind 'a presented instructor token', but an instructor SESSION is obtainable without presenting one, so any LAN or WireGuard participant can read the beacon before reveal. Sources: docs/WEB_HOSTING_AND_IDENTITY_PLAN.md section 2 (2026-09-09) and a five-service auth audit on 2026-09-13. Verified present in the working tree at commit 6690d35.
issues.fix: Remove the shortcut branch entirely. An instructor session must require the configured token or a rostered instructor credential. Add a regression test asserting that /join/ADMIN, /join/INSTRUCTOR and POST /api/auth/login with those codes all return 401 while CAPVSAR_TOKEN_INSTRUCTOR is set. Fixed 2026-09-13 (commit 944f093). The ADMIN/INSTRUCTOR shortcut is removed from authenticate_code(); an instructor authenticates with a roster credential or the configured token like every other role.
issues.verify: GET /join/ADMIN and /join/INSTRUCTOR return 401/redirect-to-error with an instructor token configured; no session row is created; the truth-leak regression in tests/test_console.py still passes. Verified by reproducing the attack against the fixed console: /join/ADMIN, /join/INSTRUCTOR and the case variant /join/admin are all refused with no session cookie set, and POST /api/auth/login with those codes returns 401. Covered by BackdoorCodeTests in tests/test_setup_auth.py, including the specific path from /join/ADMIN to beacon truth.

issues.title: enforce() fails open and /api/auth/me reports instructor to anonymous callers
issues.problem: access.enforce() returns (allowing the call) when no matching env token is configured and no session is active - an explicit 'open for local dev' branch. Every gated mutating endpoint therefore accepts anonymous requests in that state. .env.example ships all three CAPVSAR_TOKEN_* values blank, so the default deployment is unauthenticated; main.py logs a warning naming the open roles but starts anyway. Compounding it, GET /api/auth/me actively reports {authenticated: true, role: instructor} to any anonymous caller in the same state, so the UI renders full instructor controls for a stranger. Sources: docs/WEB_HOSTING_AND_IDENTITY_PLAN.md section 2 (2026-09-09) and a five-service auth audit on 2026-09-13. Verified present in the working tree at commit 6690d35.
issues.fix: Deny by default. enforce() must raise when it cannot positively identify a satisfying session or token. Gate the dev convenience behind an explicit opt-in flag (e.g. CAPVSAR_DEV_OPEN=1) that is refused when a production marker is set, and fail startup rather than warn when required identity configuration is missing. /api/auth/me must return authenticated:false when there is no session. Fixed 2026-09-13 (commit 944f093). enforce() now denies when no credential is configured instead of returning. Opening the console is deliberate via CAPVSAR_DEV_OPEN, refused when CAPVSAR_ENV is production. /api/auth/me no longer claims an instructor identity for anonymous callers.
issues.verify: With all CAPVSAR_TOKEN_* unset and no dev flag, the app refuses to start; with the dev flag, a startup banner states it. Anonymous POST to a gated route returns 403. /api/auth/me returns authenticated:false with no session. Verified: anonymous POST /api/scenarios returns 403 with tokens configured and 503 with none; /api/auth/me reports authenticated false. Covered by DenyByDefaultTests, including that CAPVSAR_DEV_OPEN is honoured only outside production. Two suites that had been passing on the fail-open were corrected rather than relaxed. 140 tests and 23 subtests pass.

issues.title: Session cookie lacks Secure, session id is returned to JavaScript, and a GET creates the session
issues.problem: Three separate weaknesses in one flow. (1) The capvsar_session cookie is set httponly/samesite=lax but WITHOUT secure=True, and because exercise :8700 stays published in plaintext alongside Caddy (see O-8) the cookie crosses the wire in the clear on the default path. (2) POST /api/auth/login also returns session_id in the JSON body, handing JavaScript a bearer secret that httponly was meant to withhold. (3) GET /join/{code} is a state-changing request that creates a session and sets a cookie - no POST confirmation and no CSRF protection, and the code sits in the URL path where it lands in browser history and proxy logs. access.py additionally accepts the session id as a ?session= query parameter. Sources: docs/WEB_HOSTING_AND_IDENTITY_PLAN.md section 2 (2026-09-09) and a five-service auth audit on 2026-09-13. Verified present in the working tree at commit 6690d35.
issues.fix: Set secure=True on the session cookie once TLS is the only path (sequence with O-8). Stop returning session_id in the login response body. Make /join/{code} render a confirmation page and require a CSRF-protected POST to consume the code. Remove ?session= and ?token= query-parameter acceptance for hosted deployment.
issues.verify: Login response body carries no session id; the cookie has Secure; GET /join/{code} creates no session row until the POST; query-parameter auth is rejected.

issues.title: Roster codes are guessable, sessions are stored unhashed, and roster regeneration does not revoke them
issues.problem: save_exercise_setup() generates participant codes that are sequential and derived from public callsigns - INSTR-1, PLT-423, OBS-423, SCN-423, MRO-1, UDF-1 - so anyone who knows the aircraft callsign can guess the aircrew and instructor codes, and codes are matched case-insensitively. A per-row random token column is generated and stored but never read by any code path, so the one unguessable credential in the schema is dead. Separately, session ids are stored in the sessions table in plaintext rather than hashed, expired rows are filtered on read but never deleted so the table grows without bound, and save_exercise_setup() does DELETE FROM roster without cascading to sessions - regenerating a roster invalidates every code while leaving the sessions minted from them valid for their full 24 hours. Sources: docs/WEB_HOSTING_AND_IDENTITY_PLAN.md section 2 (2026-09-09) and a five-service auth audit on 2026-09-13. Verified present in the working tree at commit 6690d35.
issues.fix: Make the stored per-row token the actual credential and make codes non-guessable, or require the token alongside the code. Hash session ids at rest. Delete expired sessions on a schedule. Cascade roster regeneration and membership removal to session revocation, and re-validate role on each request rather than trusting the role copied into the session.
issues.verify: Regenerating a roster terminates sessions derived from the old roster within the target window; expired rows are pruned; no plaintext session id is recoverable from the database.

issues.title: POST /api/radio/ics mutates shared radio state with no authorization
issues.problem: POST /api/radio/ics changes shared ICS and channel state for the whole exercise and carries no access.enforce() call and no session check. Any participant, or any host that can reach :8700, can rewrite the net structure mid-exercise. Neighbouring radio reads (/api/radio/config, /api/radio/rx) are likewise ungated, and the /ws and /api/radio/stream sockets authenticate with a same-origin header check that is skipped entirely when Origin is absent, which is the normal case for a non-browser client. Sources: docs/WEB_HOSTING_AND_IDENTITY_PLAN.md section 2 (2026-09-09) and a five-service auth audit on 2026-09-13. Verified present in the working tree at commit 6690d35.
issues.fix: Gate POST /api/radio/ics behind base_or_instructor. Establish identity - not just origin - on /ws and /api/radio/stream, and recheck membership periodically during an open socket so revocation propagates.
issues.verify: Anonymous POST /api/radio/ics returns 403; a non-browser client with no Origin header is rejected from /ws rather than admitted.

issues.title: Flight planner is an unauthenticated confused deputy holding instructor credentials
issues.problem: The planner holds CAPVSAR_TOKEN_INSTRUCTOR and CAPVSAR_TOKEN_BASE in its own environment and attaches them to server-side POSTs into the exercise console via _console_headers(). It has no sessions, no login and no import of access.py; only 2 of its 21 routes check anything, and that check accepts either a matching token OR merely an Origin header whose netloc equals the request host, which a non-browser client sets freely. An unauthenticated caller who can reach the planner can therefore create scenarios and broadcast messages to every console with INSTRUCTOR privilege. The fallback at app.py:1141 makes it worse: a missing _BASE token silently falls back to the _INSTRUCTOR token, so a misconfiguration escalates rather than fails. This is an architectural property, not a dev shortcut - putting single sign-on in front of the planner does not fix it, because the privilege comes from a server-held credential rather than from the caller. Sources: docs/WEB_HOSTING_AND_IDENTITY_PLAN.md section 2 (2026-09-09) and a five-service auth audit on 2026-09-13. Verified present in the working tree at commit 6690d35.
issues.fix: Propagate the CALLER's identity to the console instead of presenting a server-held credential: accept the participant session on the planner, and either forward it or exchange it for a short-lived scoped token bound to that user, exercise and operation. Remove the _BASE to _INSTRUCTOR fallback so a missing token fails closed. Authenticate the planner's own mutating routes.
issues.verify: An unauthenticated planner request cannot cause any console write. A caller holding only aircrew rights cannot create a scenario. Removing CAPVSAR_TOKEN_BASE produces an error, never an instructor-privileged call.

issues.title: AI Pilot web deck binds 0.0.0.0:8088 with no auth and permissive CORS
issues.problem: web_server.py binds 0.0.0.0:8088 by default with no authentication on any route, and returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every JSON response with a matching permissive do_OPTIONS. Any website loaded in any browser on the network can therefore read and drive it cross-origin. The mutating endpoints are consequential: POST /api/board/raw overwrites docs/BOARD.md wholesale, /api/board/task and /api/board/toggle rewrite the agent dispatch queue that Claude, Codex and Gemini execute from, /api/chat drives the LLM agent, and /api/fdr/start|stop|analyze control the flight data recorder. This is an ENGINEERING surface, not a participant one, and it is a different trust domain from the exercise console: it should not be placed behind the participant portal. It is also not containerized and not in docker-compose, so deploy-time hardening does not reach it. maneuver_server.py on 127.0.0.1:8089 is bound to loopback, which is its only real control; it has an Origin and content-type check plus a lease gate, but no identity. Sources: docs/WEB_HOSTING_AND_IDENTITY_PLAN.md section 2 (2026-09-09) and a five-service auth audit on 2026-09-13. Verified present in the working tree at commit 6690d35. SEPARATELY OBSERVED 2026-09-13: the same two response paths send no cache headers at all and reply HTTP/1.0 - _send_json() (web_server.py:58-68) and _send_file() (web_server.py:70-87) set no Cache-Control, ETag or Last-Modified. With nothing telling it otherwise a browser may serve /api/board from cache heuristically, so the board UI can show stale data and the Refresh Board button appears to do nothing. This was reproduced against a live board tab where the disk, the API and the served page all agreed at 9 tasks. The failure is silent in both directions because fetchBoard() (static/board.html:558-566) swallows a failed fetch into console.error and returns, leaving the last-rendered board on screen with no indication it has stopped updating - the UI cannot distinguish 'nothing changed' from 'I am showing you a cached or failed answer'.
issues.fix: Bind 127.0.0.1 by default and require an explicit flag to expose it. Replace ACAO:* with an exact allowlist. Require a locally configured credential on all mutating routes, especially /api/board/raw. Keep the deck on the management/WireGuard path rather than the participant front door. Note access.py cannot be reused as-is: it is FastAPI-coupled and reads the exercise SQLite database, while this is a stdlib http.server. ALSO IN SCOPE (same functions, one edit): send Cache-Control: no-store on every /api/* response from _send_json(), and appropriate caching headers from _send_file(); and give the board UI a visible staleness indicator - surface a failed or stale fetch in the page (last-updated timestamp plus an explicit error state) rather than only console.error.
issues.verify: Default start binds loopback only; a cross-origin page cannot read /api/board; POST /api/board/raw without the credential returns 403; BOARD.md is unchanged after an unauthenticated attempt. Additionally: curl -D- /api/board shows Cache-Control: no-store; a board tab left open reflects a task added by another client within one poll interval without a manual reload; and with the server stopped, the page visibly indicates it is not updating instead of silently showing the last good render.

issues.title: No single front door: Caddy fronts one backend and is bypassable on the LAN
issues.problem: The Caddy container is a single-purpose proxy - reverse_proxy exercise:8700, with tls internal and site names hardcoded to ms01, ms01.local and 192.0.2.151 - existing to give tablets a trusted secure context for microphone access. flightplanner has no TLS front at all and is not in the Caddyfile. Because exercise :8700 and flightplanner :8090 remain published as plaintext HTTP on the LAN, the TLS front is bypassable and the non-Secure session cookie and any header or query-parameter token cross the wire in the clear on the default path. firewall.sh notes that Docker's iptables rules precede ufw's, so ufw does not filter published container ports and the router forward list is the real boundary. There is consequently no one place a user can log in once and reach the console, the mission base view and the planner. Sources: docs/WEB_HOSTING_AND_IDENTITY_PLAN.md section 2 (2026-09-09) and a five-service auth audit on 2026-09-13. Verified present in the working tree at commit 6690d35. INVESTIGATED 2026-09-13: path-mounting the planner behind one hostname is NOT viable without changing the planner first, which is what the identity plan warned about when it said to use a separate subdomain if the planner's URL construction makes path mounting brittle.
